_what: Phase 3 step 3.3 of road-to-frontend-fidelity-calibration. The instance that makes AC-3 checkable: every dimension the Phase 2 schema accounts for is either shipped with >=1 row or carries a four-field null_record naming the pre-registered falsifier that fired. Dimension ids and falsifier ids come from agents/evidence/analysis/frontend-fidelity-preregistered-falsifiers.md; claim ids (A1..A13) from frontend-fidelity-assertion-inventory.md.
surface: this suite's own frontend surface (src/skills, src/rules, work_engine ui directives)

dimensions._note: The one dimension the 2.3 prediction said would ship. Detector wired in step 3.1; scope enforced by the shared audit-membership predicate.

Shipped as a coverage measurement over a documented set, exactly as 2.3 pre-registered it — NOT as a runtime number. The rows below measure which widths the review is told to test, which is a fact about a file and is stable across reads.

null_record.unavailable_capability: a page-reaching capture primitive on the host the fixtures run on — no browser driver, no headless capture, and no MCP browser tool is wired to the fixture harness here
null_record.reopening_condition: a page-reaching capture primitive is confirmed available on the fixture host, at which point the render-dependent fixtures are un-skipped against it and this dimension returns to the matrix with real rows

dimensions._note: Cut, with all four claims it covers enumerated. This is the dimension b-page-capture-primitive resolved (option b) and the reason F0-uncapturable had to be pre-registered: F1-F3 all presuppose a run that cannot be attempted.

null_record.unavailable_capability: any check that can see what a surface presents INSTEAD of motion — grep proves a prefers-reduced-motion block exists, never that the block presents an alternative rather than setting animation: none
null_record.reopening_condition: a check exists that can read the declarations inside a prefers-reduced-motion block and distinguish a presented alternative from a suppression; step 9.3 closes the PROSE half of this gap and deliberately does not reopen the measurement half

dimensions._note: Cut on the pre-registered falsifier, not on difficulty. The only obtainable number is a presence count, and no finding about the claim can be derived from it.

rows._note: From the seeded fixture tests/design-artifacts/fixtures/token-detector/seeded-raw-literal.json. In scope because the audit holds a token whose value is exactly this literal.

expectation_source.ref: no audit bucket holds this value — outside the pre-registered dimension

rows._note: The F4-unscoped guard, recorded as a row rather than omitted. The detector does NOT emit a finding here, and the clean fixture asserts that. Recording it as `unspecified` is the difference between a scoped detector and a silent one: expected is null because no source specifies a value, so there is nothing to deviate from.

rows.expected: 320px present in the measured viewport set

expectation_source.ref: src/skills/fe-design/SKILL.md:213 — "every layout must work on 320px width"

rows._note: Post step 5.2. The pre-state observed value was `1440px, 768px, 375px` and this row was a deviation; the fix put the asserted floor into the set a reviewer is told to test.
A row rather than an absence, which is the whole point of the `unmeasured` status: a reader can tell a dimension that was blocked from one nobody thought of.
